newsitem.title: USA: Amtech to terminate Korean joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Amtech to terminate Korean joint venture.

text.p: Amtech Systems Inc said on Wednesday that it had reached an agreement to terminate its Korean joint venture.
Amtech said it is to receive $478,143 as a return of its initial $500,000 investment and reimbursement of certain direct and indirect expenses.

About one year ago, Amtech Systems entered into a joint venture agreement, giving it 45 percent ownership interest and a 50 percent voting interest in the joint venture company Seil Semicon Inc, in return for its commitment to invest up to $500,000 in cash.
The purpose of the joint venture was to operate a silicon test wafer reclaiming business through Seil, which remains in the start-up phase, Amtech said.

Amtech said a recent review of anticipated costs during the start-up phase and the additional equipment required for the operations increased the total projected capital requirements by about $2.5 million. Under the existing ownership structure, Amtech was Seil's only source for these additional funds.
Amtech said that increasing its investment to $3 million was more risk than the company should take. Amtech said this was the primary reason for the termination.
